title: Explicit expression and fast algorithms for the inverse of some matrices arising from implicit time integration

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Equation (2.18) states H^T = F [[0, c_0^T], [c_0, C_n]], where C_n = diag(c_1, ..., c_n). However, H is defined in (1.1) with subdiagonal entries 1, 2, ..., n, so H^T has superdiagonal entries 1, 2, ..., n. The product F [[0, c_0^T], [c_0, C_n]] would give superdiagonal entries c_1, ..., c_n (the Gauss/Radau nodes), which are not equal to 1, 2, ..., n in general. The subsequent derivation in the proof of Theorem 2.4 (line 386) correctly uses D_n = diag(1, 2, ..., n) instead of C_n, confirming this is a typographical error in (2.18) rather than a mathematical one. The correct identity should be H^T = F [[0, c_0^T], [c_0, D_n]].

summary:
The paper presents an explicit expression for the inverse of matrices of the form W = V^{-1}HV, with applications to implicit Runge-Kutta and block implicit methods. Three fast O(n²) algorithms are presented for computing the matrix elements. The verification examined 59 snippets across all sections, equations, theorems, proofs, algorithms, tables, and figures.

One minor issue was identified: equation (2.18) contains a notational inconsistency where C_n (diagonal matrix of quadrature nodes) is written instead of D_n (diagonal matrix of integers 1,...,n). The subsequent derivation in the proof of Theorem 2.4 correctly uses D_n, confirming this is a typographical error in (2.18) rather than a mathematical flaw. The correction is: H^T = F [[0, c_0^T], [c_0, D_n]] instead of H^T = F [[0, c_0^T], [c_0, C_n]].

The symbolic and numerical verification results confirm the correctness of the explicit formula (3.1). The three algorithms (3.1, 3.2, 3.3) achieve the claimed O(n²) complexity, with Algorithm 3.3 providing the best numerical stability. The diagonal elements suffer from cancellation errors in floating-point arithmetic, but the authors acknowledge this limitation and show that quadruple precision addresses it. The paper is internally consistent across sections and the mathematical derivations are sound. The paper passes verification with the noted typographical issue being non-critical.
